turns.prompt_text: All right, I found some gorilla 100% all-purpose silicone
turns.response_html:
That silicone is a solid choice for a lot of different projects because it’s waterproof, shrink-proof, and stays flexible over time.

Since it is "100% silicone," there are a few things to keep in mind while you're working with it:

  • Prep the Surface: Make sure the area is completely clean and dry. Silicone doesn't bond well to old caulk, dust, or grease.
  • Ventilation: It usually has a strong vinegar-like smell (acetic acid) while curing, so it's best to have a window open or a fan running.
  • The "Skin" Time: You generally have about 5 to 10 minutes to smooth it out before it starts to form a skin. Once it starts skinning, trying to smooth it further will usually just make a mess.
  • Clean Up: Since it's waterproof, you can't clean it up with water. You’ll need mineral spirits or a dry cloth to wipe away any excess before it dries.
  • Non-Paintable: Keep in mind that paint will not stick to 100% silicone. If you're using it on something that needs to be painted later, you'll want to make sure the silicone is the very last step.

What are you planning on using it for? Knowing the specific project can help determine if this particular formula is the best fit.
